name: Mazarine Blue
lede: Mazarine Blue is an old name for a rich blue, possibly honoring a French cardinal; the modern swatch is much lighter than the word suggests.

sections.title: A cardinal's blue?
sections.body:
Paterson defines mazarine blue as a dark, rich blue, and passes on Partridge's suggestion that the name comes from Cardinal Mazarin (1602-1661), Richelieu's successor as France's chief minister [1]. That is a hedged derivation and the other books do not confirm it. Maerz and Paul record the name from 1686, on plate 44 [2].

The swatch tells a different story from the words. Ridgway 1912 (plate IX) and ISCC-NBS 1955 (block 197) gave a light, soft blue, here with a lightness of 73 [2]. So the dictionary's "dark rich" and the standard samples disagree [1][2]. The books do not say which of them the name first meant.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Mazarine Blue is rare in painting: 19 of 23,781 paintings, 0.08%, cover at least 5% of their canvas with it, as photographed [3]. The top match is Jongkind's view of Paris (1853), about 30% [3]. Its nearest standard name is [[periwinkle]], 8.5 ΔE away [2]. Related names: [[sky-blue]], [[light-blue]], [[royal-blue]] and [[midnight-blue]].

questions.q: How does Paterson describe mazarine blue?

openers: Mazarine blue may honor Cardinal Mazarin (1602-1661), though Paterson only says possibly.
